Reproduced WS 502 after hot replacement of Logic while Comet/Job kept running. Recorded original run_id recovery and unchanged tool transcripts. Comet readiness was 0; during replacement Docker DNS briefly returned upstream synthetic addresses for missing logic, then the correct container IP. The cold-maintenance activation procedure is being corrected; no auth or retry bypass.

Later DLQ check exposed missing actor_user_id in recovered Router metadata: the existing strict room broker receipt rejected it. Fixed only the authorized metadata assignment, leaving receipt validation intact.

limitations: Same machine, native platform, original Runtime paths/profile/endpoints and dependency fingerprints only; no cross-machine migration or actual OS reboot.
Native helper death uses actual Windows process termination with the IM boundary stubbed; it is a contract supplement, not full Docker failure E2E.
Model scenario uses three HTTP/WebSocket clients, not browser acceptance; browser evidence remains a separate stage.
Controlled event/status receipt loss, read-only native tools; not proof for arbitrary side-effecting tool execution or a natural network outage.
Windows shared storage does not establish OS read-only mounts or ACL migration.
CANN/private Agent/cross-room extra regressions, clean Linux install, GHCR publication and Release acceptance remain separate.
Agent activation after a cold batch must cold-restart the restored IM stack without deleting volumes; arbitrary hot replacement availability is not covered.
Already-completed historical bad records missing actor are not rewritten; preserve their publication and audit separately. No ledger reset or relaxed receipt validation.

activation_diagnostic.actual_dns_probe: During Logic removal, socket.getaddrinfo(logic,9100) returned 198.18.1.223 and 2001:2::1c1; two seconds later it returned the actual 172.23.0.10. Comet stream readiness remained 0 during the observation.
activation_diagnostic.gateway_error: EOF / HTTP 502 during the same maintenance window
activation_diagnostic.scope: The probe observes a real DNS/reconnect outage. It does not prove a permanent gRPC cache failure or fix arbitrary hot container replacement.
